chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who gives charity to a stranger in the form of part of his house, and then the donor dies. He said: 'That is appraised at its value, and its price is paid to him (the heir).'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a charitable gift of real estate when the donor dies?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a partial gift (hibah) to a non-heir, ruling that the donated portion is treated as a debt against the estate rather than remaining in kind. Consequently, the heirs receive the appraised monetary value, ensuring the donor's estate is settled fairly before distribution. This highlights the Shia juristic distinction between full ownership transfer during life and the financial settlement upon death.
